slides.title: Scientific Liquidity Agents: An Agent-Based Model of Knowledge Arbitrage in Scientific Communities
slides.highlight: This paper introduces an agent-based model simulating how scientific knowledge moves between domains via specialized agents and arbitrageurs, offering a framework for modeling meso-scale knowledge transfer dynamics relevant to MIMIC's goal of simulating harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Agent-based model simulating knowledge arbitrage, revealing verification as the primary bottleneck in scientific communities.
card.key_idea: Simulates specialists and arbitrageurs using BDI architecture, prerequisite graphs, and publication registries to model knowledge liquidity.
card.evaluation: Two exploratory simulations (10/18 agents) analyzed via contact networks, problem graphs, and replication success rates.
card.limitation: Highly stylized synthetic environment with small agent counts; lacks empirical calibration and real-world content transfer.

slides.title: Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics
slides.tldr: LLM AGENT STABILITY VARIES BY MODEL
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that alignment drift in LLM-based opinion dynamics is model-specific and interaction-induced, highlighting the need for careful agent selection in MIMIC's simulations of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLM choice dictates opinion dynamics outcomes, revealing model-specific alignment drift during simulated discussions.
card.key_idea: Framework quantifies LLM-specific alignment drift via theory-free psychometric measurements and classical opinion dynamics model fitting.
card.evaluation: Six LLMs tested on two policy issues with no-discussion controls; results show model-specific dispersion and homophily patterns.
card.limitation: Limited to economic policy topics, English prompts, and proprietary models; single-axis measurement ignores multi-dimensional values.

slides.title: A Study on the Effects of Finger Movements on a Humanoid Hugging Robot
slides.highlight: This study examines how finger movement patterns in hugging robots influence user perceptions, finding that repetitive and asynchronous movements enhance sensations while simultaneous movements evoke care.

card.one_liner: Finger movement patterns in hugging robots significantly influence users' psychological perceptions of care and intent.
card.key_idea: Developed a semi-humanoid robot with independently driven fingers to test how movement patterns (simultaneous/asynchronous, repetitive) affect user emotions.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects experiments with 20 participants using 7-point Likert scales; analyzed via t-tests and ANOVA, showing significant effects on perceived care.
card.limitation: Small sample size (n=20) and short duration limit generalizability; ethical risks of excessive dependency or inappropriate intimacy remain unaddressed.

slides.title: Just Between Us? Exploring a Wearable-Mediated Channel for Discreet Human-Agent Interaction in a Shared Game Setting
slides.highlight: This study explores a wearable-mediated channel combining in-ear audio and head tilts for discreet human-agent interaction in shared settings, addressing challenges in social robot communication where public speech or gestures are insufficient.

card.one_liner: Wearable-mediated discreet interaction enables private human-agent communication in shared games without increasing wearer tension.
card.key_idea: Combines in-ear audio for agent messages with head-tilt detection for responses, enabling bidirectional discreet interaction in a three-player card game.
card.evaluation: Wizard-of-Oz study with 40 participants; measured protocol consistency, wearer pressure/tension, and usability via questionnaires and interviews.
card.limitation: Wizard-of-Oz setup lacks autonomous agent intelligence; results may not generalize to real-world social robots or complex environments.

slides.title: Realbotix Unveils Armless Tabletop Humanoid Torsos
slides.highlight: Realbotix has introduced armless tabletop humanoid torsos priced at $11,950, offering a compact form factor for human-robot interaction research.

slides.title: Persona AI Brings Calm Experience to Humanoid Startups
slides.highlight: Persona AI is developing calm humanoid experiences, relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
slides.highlight: This paper presents an open smart-ring platform that integrates multimodal sensing (speech, gesture, physiological) to enable timely and effective human-robot interaction, offering insights relevant to embodied social robotics.

card.one_liner: OpenZilo is an open smart-ring platform linking multimodal sensing to robot execution for human-centric interaction.
card.key_idea: Integrates microphone, IMU, PPG, and temperature sensors with a modular software architecture separating acquisition, event interpretation, and robot execution.
card.evaluation: Tested with 10 participants on speech/gesture commands and simulated physiological events; achieved ~90% task success rates using descriptive metrics.
card.limitation: Relies on simulated physiological events and a small convenience sample; lacks statistical significance tests and real-world clinical validation.

slides.title: When Does GenAI Use Support Critical Thinking? A Cross-Cultural Structural Account of Transactive Memory with GenAI
slides.tldr: TMS STRUCTURE FOR GENAI CRITICAL THINKING
slides.highlight: This study applies Transactive Memory Systems theory to human-AI partnerships, showing that critical thinking in GenAI-assisted work depends on how cognitive labor is divided and coordinated rather than mere tool exposure. It provides a structural framework for understanding engagement dynamics in hybrid teams, relevant to modeling social perception of human-AI collaboration.

card.one_liner: Critical thinking in GenAI use depends on coordinating cognitive labor and actively reworking output, not just exposure.
card.key_idea: Structural equation modeling tests how confidence and familiarity drive specialization, coordination, and reflective transformation to predict critical thinking.
card.evaluation: Survey of 891 US and Turkish students; SEM showed structural invariance across cultures, with experience affecting thinking only via specific behaviors.
card.limitation: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; reliance on self-reported binary outcome and convenience sampling may introduce bias.

slides.title: User Attributes and Political Ideology Shape LLM Receptiveness in Online Political Debates
slides.highlight: This study reveals that LLMs exhibit systematic receptiveness asymmetries based on user political ideology and expertise in multi-turn debates, which is critical for HyECHO's goal of modeling fair and accurate social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: LLMs systematically favor left-leaning users in political debates, regardless of stance or expertise.
card.key_idea: Reconstructed Debate.org and controlled multi-turn simulations measure LLM receptiveness to varying user political orientations, expertise, and rhetoric.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 5,376 debates and 150,000 simulations across four models, using logistic regressions and human-validated LLM annotations for adoption rates.
card.limitation: Asymmetry is model-dependent and can be erased or reversed by fine-tuning on different political corpora.

slides.title: InteractionBench: Measuring Timing, Task Accuracy, Whisper and Volume, and Grounding in Real-Time Voice Systems
slides.highlight: This paper introduces InteractionBench, a benchmark evaluating real-time voice systems on conversational timing, spoken-task accuracy, whisper/volume control, and groundedness, which aligns with HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and group norms in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: InteractionBench evaluates real-time voice systems on timing, task accuracy, paralinguistics, and groundedness using unified audio.
card.key_idea: A unified harness streams identical synthetic audio to seven systems, scoring four dimensions via rule-based timing checks and LLM judges.
card.evaluation: Tested seven systems (hosted, open, cascade) on 221 items; hosted models outperform open ones in groundedness and task accuracy.
card.limitation: Timing scores for hosted systems include network latency, and protocol inconsistencies (e.g., interruption timing) hinder direct cross-system comparison.

slides.title: When Architectural Spaces Start to Act
slides.highlight: This paper explores how architectural robots reshape spatial conditions, extending human-robot interaction beyond momentary actions to long-term inhabitation and control, which informs the design of embodied environments for social robots.

card.one_liner: Architectural robots shape long-term spatial conditions, requiring new interaction models beyond transient motion.
card.key_idea: Interaction extends to persistent spatial configurations, creating challenges for shared occupancy, perceived control, and multi-robot coordination.
card.evaluation: Qualitative reflection drawing on prior co-design studies and in-the-wild experiments with robotic partitions and benches.
card.limitation: Lacks quantitative data on long-term inhabitation; relies on speculative design scenarios rather than deployed systems.

slides.title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
slides.highlight: This work presents a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system where learned models propose actions but symbolic rules and validated physics enforce safety limits, directly addressing the need for trustworthy, verifiable agent architectures in complex societal simulations.

card.one_liner: GURU uses symbolic rules to verify learned model proposals for safe mission-critical automation.
card.key_idea: Hierarchical neuro-symbolic agents propose actions, but a symbolic engine enforces hard limits before validated physics executes them.
card.evaluation: Tested on CFD, space awareness, and reactor tasks; improved simulation rates and risk scoring vs. baselines with low variance.
card.limitation: Requires validated physics models and strict symbolic rule definitions, limiting applicability to domains with hard-coded safety constraints.

slides.title: A Framework for Task-Agnostic Counterfactual Fairness in Transformers through Activation Steering
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a framework using mechanistic interpretability to enforce counterfactual fairness in transformers via activation steering, offering a task-agnostic method to mitigate bias in automated decision-making systems.

card.one_liner: MICF unifies mechanistic interpretability and counterfactual fairness to mitigate transformer bias via activation steering.
card.key_idea: Reformulates counterfactual fairness constraints using mechanistic interpretability to identify and steer sensitive attribute activations in transformers.
card.evaluation: Tested on UTICalc and COMPAS datasets using TabPFN; measured counterfactual fairness scores, accuracy, and causal effects against baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-generated counterfactuals and linear representation assumptions, which may fail under feature superposition or complex confounding.

slides.title: HiPaper: A Human-AI Collaborative System for Academic Literature Triage and Scholarly Sensemaking
slides.highlight: HiPaper demonstrates a human-in-the-loop workflow for scholarly sensemaking that exposes intermediate AI outputs for user inspection and revision, offering a model for transparent hybrid collaboration.

card.one_liner: HiPaper supports scholarly sensemaking via a three-stage human-AI workflow exposing intermediate outputs for user inspection.
card.key_idea: A human-in-the-loop system organizing literature review into Retrieval, Collection, and Synthesis stages with a persistent Knowledge Pocket workspace.
card.evaluation: User study with 14 Ph.D. students using SUS, NASA-TLX, and behavioral logs; showed efficient support across familiar and unfamiliar domains.
card.limitation: Small sample size (14 Ph.D. students) from a single institution limits generalizability to broader academic populations.
